text.insert: Workers receive accepted, worker-facing standards as instructions for authored source. Checks then evaluate their output. A standard should identify its lint rules or its review mechanism so a reader can tell which requirements are automatically enforced.

steps.text: Include the worker-facing rules in boot context
Run associated lint checks against the proposed source changes
Review requirements without automated checks explicitly
Preserve findings and gate the handoff on the required checks

text.insert: Worker boot, librarian passes, and dashboard previews pass the selected game to the standards loader. The loader resolves that game's source registry and does not fall back to Melee when its standards are absent. This selects a game-owned baseline; it does not compose shared and game-specific rule sets automatically.

The review_lint diff scan loads the selected game's rule slices, scans their declared file patterns, and reports the associated standard_id. It fails closed if the scanner cannot run. File patterns come from the rules, so C++ and header checks are not excluded by a C-only prefilter. Slices can provide post-scan validation hooks. Accepted status alone does not create an automated check; upstream formatting and build regression checks remain separate requirements.

SMS's project slice rejects vendor edits, recognized dummy padding, declaration rename candidates, and new identifier macro aliases. Naming findings require human review, with approved changes integrated separately into the accepted base. Text checks do not prove complete C++ rename detection or identify every disguised padding tactic. Workers must also preserve names and supply evidence for map research, inline reconstruction, and remaining frame differences.

For each changed game C++ source file, the SMS post-scan hook requires a mapped object, checks Ninja freshness, and runs tools/validate-symbol-order.py. Patch-only scans fail this requirement because they cannot supply built evidence. HEAD-only scans also require a clean checkout. Missing objects, stale inputs, and validator failures block the gate. Successful validator output is retained as an informational finding, including upstream UNUSED-size warnings for explicit review. Header-only changes still require separate validation of affected translation units.

Librarians see standards for recognition so a mandated code shape is not mistaken for an inferred developer convention. They do not publish or change standards through semantic proposals. A person authors and reviews those changes.

rows: Accepted, worker-facing standards from the selected game. Melee retains five-rule compact and two-rule minimal summaries; other games retain their full baseline at every budget.
Enforced, not injected: review_lint findings carry the violated standard_id; the scan fails closed
Recognition only: id, title, summary of accepted standards, so a standard-mandated code shape is not mistaken for a developer convention
GET /api/standards returns records, examples, the effective XML, context, inventory, and warnings; POST applies one validated edit
